glance_takeaway: The page is a research summary titled 'murmur' about bioacoustics -- recognizing one bird species through cheap, physically-plausible audio noise/augmentation. The main message is that cheap 'reverb-flavoured' data augmentation partially works: it delivers a +5.9 point gain (val macro-F1 0.612 -> 0.671), but the lift lands on common species while the rare tail barely moves. The underlying bet was to hold a small CNN fixed and change only the augmentation, testing whether near-free reverb transforms beat a bigger backbone when data is scarce. An experiment ledger charts variants (baseline 0.612, +light reverb 0.641, +pitch/stretch 0.589 regression, +noise mix 0.643, full stack 0.671 best, heavy reverb 0.663).
